newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares revive, more advances up to U.S..
newsitem.headline: Danish shares revive, more advances up to U.S..

text.p: Danish share prices closed slightly higher on Wednesday, aided and abetted by the strong dollar, with dealers foreseeing more gains ahead provided the Dow remains in its present positive mood.
"If the positive trend on Wall street continues and the dollar stays high, we should advance again tomorrow," one dealer said.

The KFX top-20 index gained 0.34 point to close at 188.80 in overall bourse turnover of 1.287 billion crowns. The KFX August future rose 0.75 point to 189.40 with 288 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
It was a decline in Novo Nordisk which prevented the index from climbing further.

Hit by a major foreign sales order, the Novo share closed 10 crowns down at 730 on fears about falling insulin sales in the United States ahead of the biotechnology group's first-half 1997 result due August 13.
In contrast A.P. Moeller's D/S Svendborg soared 9,000 crowns to a closing 435,000, its highest point this year.
Twin D/S 1912 also did well, putting on 4,000 to finish at 300,000.
